Those who remember the enjoyable match on the track last summer will not doubt welcome this opportunity of meeting them again over the country. Prominent among their runners is A. Kench, who is also a member of our own Club.

The Ten Miles Championship, the 43rd of the series, was preceded by a race over five miles, open to Juniors under 21 years of age on the date of the race. Our team did not shine in finishing 17th, but A. Kench once again gave signs of developing into a very useful runner.
Our five miles course was used and Joe Flower won from A. Kench, who was running for Old Emanuel A.C., and is, of course, a members of our Club.
A surprise was caused by the prominent position (5th) occupied by Alfred Kench, one of our younger runners whose promise has been commented upon from time to time in these columns.
Our 'bus left Westminster shortly after 10-30 a.m. and we made for Clapham Common, where Jack Flower, our first man, would hand on to Alfred Kench.
In the 1 Mile A. Kench, a member of our own club, was running for the Old Emanuel A.C., and he won the race in brilliant style, finishing with a positively electrifying burst down the straight.

In the 4 x 880 yards we scored an easy win in slow time, Alf Kench running a fine half to give us a good lead which was kept to the finish. The 4 x 300 again saw us placed third, only this time Croydon beat Mitcham.

Alf Kench ran well in the 440 yards, winning his heat in 51 4-5 seconds, and finishing third in the second round to Wolff and Skinner. This was won in 50 1-5 secs. and it seemed that our man had gained standard, but confirmation on this point is still lacking.
